why: The first package rung asked once more, now under ADR 0066: a creature buys one package an opportunity, so the two picks of a round no longer stack on one creature. Search 9 (#181) found a set that beats stun-first 0.7675 to 0.0125 on seeds it never saw, but it priced a game where greedy put both picks on one creature in half its opportunities, and that game is gone: the greedy mirror went from one 6-round match played 400 times to matches of 6 to 13 rounds, and the lookahead went from beating greedy 0.755 to losing to it 0.383. The content is `4d7a841c`, the same as search 9, so this run and that one differ by ADR 0066 alone. Nothing else moves: the same panel (greedy, stun-first, random, ranking last a candidate that falls below the start against any), the same check (search-4), the same start (the built-in weights) and the same budget and seed. What would make it a rung: a set that beats stun-first on seeds it never saw, under the new rule. The tell to read first: search 9's pairs against greedy were all won by the same seat both times, because a mirrored pair shares its seed and so its d20 rolls; if that holds again the greedy column is a constant and the search is ranked by the other two.
